title: Build a Trust-Safe Citation Verifier
summary: Build a working, governed system that catches fabricated, mis-stated, and unsupported citations before they ship. Async course with a built-in AI tutor. No coding background needed.
audience: Researchers, writers, legal teams, educators, and publishers responsible for claims that must be traceable and correct.
learningPaths: Define the claim and citation contract
Test whether the source supports the claim
evidence: Primary sources and authoritative source records
Known-good and known-bad citation test cases
methodology: Define what the verifier must establish
Separate source existence from claim support
Return inspectable evidence for every finding
Require human review for ambiguous or consequential claims
assumptions: Learners can supply representative claims and citations
Final publication decisions remain with an accountable human
limitations: A verifier cannot guarantee that every source is complete or authoritative
Course content is educational and does not replace professional legal or editorial review

title: Build a Regulated Claims Checker
summary: Build a working tool that screens marketing, product, and label claims against the rules that apply before you publish. Async course with a built-in AI tutor.
audience: Marketing, product, compliance, and regulatory teams whose public claims may be reviewed by regulators.
learningPaths: Map claims to rules and evidence
Classify prohibited, qualified, and supportable language
evidence: Applicable statutes, regulations, and agency guidance
methodology: Identify the exact claim and audience
Compare wording with required evidence and qualifications
assumptions: The relevant jurisdiction and product category are defined
limitations: The checker supports review but does not provide legal advice or final regulatory approval

title: Build Your First AI Team, in a Weekend
summary: The on-ramp course. In one weekend, build a small, supervised AI team around one real workflow—named agents, a one-line role contract for each, and a human-approval step so nothing sends or spends without you.
audience: Founders, operators, creators, and small teams ready to move from informal prompting to one supervised AI workflow.
learningPaths: Name the agents and their jobs
methodology: Start with one useful low-risk workflow
Give every agent a bounded role
assumptions: A human owner can review every consequential output
The first workflow is bounded and reversible
limitations: Named agents do not create accountability on their own
External actions require permissions, controls, and human authorization

title: Build a Governed AI Operator
summary: Build a supervised AI that researches, drafts, and organizes in your voice and never sends, posts, or spends without your approval.
audience: Founders, executives, professionals, and creators who need leverage while retaining authority over external actions.
evidence: Versioned run, review, and approval records
assumptions: The accountable user controls credentials and approvals
Connected tools expose permissions appropriate to the workflow
limitations: No control eliminates all model or integration failures
The operator cannot replace licensed professional judgment or organizational accountability

title: Get Your Org's Knowledge AI-Ready
summary: Build a readiness checker that assesses coverage, freshness, structure, contradictions, and sensitive data, and prepares your knowledge base for safe, accurate retrieval.
audience: Teams preparing internal documents, policies, support content, or research collections for AI-assisted retrieval.
evidence: Representative retrieval questions and expected answers
methodology: Audit the source before the assistant
assumptions: Document owners can identify authoritative versions
Sensitive-data and access rules are available
limitations: Source preparation cannot guarantee perfect retrieval
Incomplete or conflicting organizational knowledge must remain visible rather than being silently resolved

title: Build a Legislative and Regulatory Tracker
summary: Build a tool that monitors bills and rules across jurisdictions, scores relevance, and summarizes each change with a citation to the primary source.
audience: Legal, policy, compliance, advocacy, and regulated-industry teams that cannot afford to miss material changes.
evidence: Versioned bill, rule, and docket records
assumptions: Official sources expose sufficient public information
Domain reviewers define materiality and relevance
limitations: No monitor guarantees immediate detection of every change
Summaries are informational and do not replace jurisdiction-specific legal advice

title: Audit Any Business for AI-Readiness
summary: Build an audit method and tool that maps workflows, scores AI-readiness, classifies risk, and outputs a defensible roadmap.
audience: Consultants, operators, transformation leaders, and internal AI owners who need a repeatable adoption method.
learningPaths: Define the business decision and audit scope
Map inputs, outputs, tools, and handoffs
Package the audit as a repeatable service
evidence: Policies, systems, authority, and failure cases
methodology: Turn findings into owned implementation steps
assumptions: Workflow owners participate and provide representative evidence
Leadership can assign accountable owners to accepted recommendations
limitations: Readiness scores are decision aids rather than guarantees
Recommendations depend on the completeness and accuracy of supplied workflow evidence
